DYNAMIC DEPENDENCY DAG CONTRACT v1.
The nodes are exactly the 48 entity names introduced by the init events below. Their two-digit numeric suffix defines the order: suffix 00 < ... < suffix 47, regardless of any domain prefix such as service-, resource-, case-, sample-, or artifact-node-. Each node has integer base, value, revision, and dirty. Directed weighted edges may only go from a lower-suffix node to a higher-suffix node, so the graph is acyclic.
init(n,b): base=value=b mod 997, revision=0, dirty=false.
link(p,c,w): require p<c; insert or replace edge p->c with weight w mod 997, then mark c and every transitive descendant dirty.
unlink(p,c): if the edge exists remove it and mark c and every transitive descendant dirty; otherwise ignore.
set_base(n,b): set base=b mod 997, increment n.revision, and mark n plus every transitive descendant dirty.
recompute(n): apply only when every direct parent is clean. Set value=(base + sum(parent.value*edge_weight)) mod 997, set dirty=false, increment revision. Otherwise ignore.
cascade(): visit all nodes in ascending order and recompute each dirty node once its parents are clean. Because all edges point upward, one ascending pass cleans every node.
checkpoint(label,S): save base,value,dirty for ordered scope S, replacing the label.
restore(label,S): restore saved base,value,dirty for nodes in both scopes and increment each restored node revision; then mark every descendant outside the restored set dirty. Ignore if intersection is empty.
Every event acknowledgement states applied/ignored but hides current values.
audit(S) returns compact JSON with requested records in the requested order (node,base,value,revision,dirty), dirty_count, and clean_value_sum_mod_997. JSON object-key order is not semantic and equivalent key ordering is accepted. No unstated side effects exist.

HIERARCHICAL QUOTA LEDGER CONTRACT v2.
The world starts empty at integer time 0. register(scope,parent,limit) creates
a scope once; parent is null or an existing scope, limit is a nonnegative
integer, and cycles are impossible. A reservation against a scope consumes
capacity from that scope and every ancestor. set_limit(scope,limit) changes a
known scope's limit when limit is nonnegative; existing usage is retained and
may therefore exceed the new limit. freeze/unfreeze(scope) toggles the known
scope. reserve(id,scope,amount,ttl) applies only when, in this precedence order:
scope exists; amount and ttl are positive integers; id is new; neither scope
nor any ancestor is frozen; and active usage plus amount is at most the limit
at every lineage scope. On success it records amount and expiry now+ttl.
release(id) deactivates a known active reservation; otherwise ignore. tick(d)
advances time only for positive integer d. A reservation is active exactly
until released or current time >= expiry. Expiry is half-open and lazy but all
usage calculations ignore expired reservations. Event acknowledgements reveal
applied/ignored and the reason, but never usage, limits, or reservation state.
hypothetical(id,scope,amount,ttl) is read-only and returns allowed, exact
reason (unknown_scope, invalid_amount, invalid_ttl, duplicate_id, frozen, or
quota_exceeded), binding_scope for quota/frozen failures, and lineage usage and
limits before the attempt. Lineage is ordered from the requested scope to
the root. When multiple lineage scopes are frozen, binding_scope is the
first (nearest) frozen scope in that order. For quota failures it is the
first (nearest) scope whose usage plus amount exceeds its limit. counterfactual_audit(omit_sequence,requests)
replays every numbered visible event from an empty world except exactly
omit_sequence, leaving all later event arguments unchanged, then returns time,
ordered hypothetical results, allowed_count, denied_count, quota_denied_count,
and frozen_denied_count. omit_sequence is one-based over events after this
contract step. JSON object-key order is nonsemantic. No unstated defaults or
side effects exist.

MVCC TRANSACTION CONTRACT v1.
init(key,value) creates a committed integer key at version 0. begin(tx,mode) starts a new epoch only when tx is absent or terminal; the first successful begin for a transaction uses epoch 0 and each later successful begin increments that transaction's prior epoch by one. mode is read_committed, snapshot, or serializable. Begin captures all committed values and versions.
write(tx,key,value) stores value mod 997 in the active transaction's local write set; otherwise ignore.
derive(tx,target,source,mul,add) is active-only. It reads source from the transaction's own write set first; otherwise read_committed uses current committed state and snapshot/serializable use the begin snapshot. It records the observed committed version for source and writes (source*mul+add) mod 997 to target.
commit(tx) is active-only. For serializable mode, abort_conflict if any externally read source's current version differs from its recorded observed version. Otherwise atomically publish local writes in key-name order, incrementing each written key version once, and set status=committed. An aborted conflict publishes nothing. snapshot and read_committed do not conflict-check.
abort(tx) discards an active transaction's local writes and sets status=aborted. Event acknowledgements reveal applied/ignored/committed/aborted/aborted_conflict and sequence, but hide values, versions, read sets, and write sets.
audit(keys,transactions) returns compact JSON: requested key,value,version records; requested transaction,status,mode,epoch,read_count,write_count records; selected_value_sum_mod_997; and committed_count, defined as the number of requested transaction records whose current status is committed. Identifier fields make requested-record ordering nonsemantic. No unstated side effects exist.

BITEMPORAL EVENT HISTORY CONTRACT v1.
System sequence is the one-based sequence printed in every event acknowledgement. Valid-time intervals are half-open [valid_from,valid_to).
put(id,entity,valid_from,valid_to,value): require a new id and valid_from<valid_to; append that record at the current system sequence. Otherwise ignore.
retract(id): if id names an existing record not previously retracted, mark its retraction at the current system sequence. Otherwise ignore.
At query as_of_system=S, a record is visible exactly when its put sequence is <=S and it has no retraction sequence <=S. A visible record covers valid_time=V exactly when valid_from<=V<valid_to.
resolve(entity,V,S): among visible covering records for entity choose the one with greatest put sequence. Return its id,value,put_sequence,valid_from,valid_to; return status=missing if none.
audit(Q) resolves every labeled query in the requested order and returns compact JSON with records, resolved_count, and resolved_value_sum_mod_997. JSON object-key order is not semantic. Event acknowledgements reveal applied/ignored and system sequence but do not reveal current resolutions. No unstated side effects exist.

INTERLEAVED SAGA CONTRACT v1.
Every resource starts with integer balance 0. A saga has status, epoch, and an epoch-local ordered step ledger.
open(s): if s does not exist, create it status=open, epoch=0, empty ledger; otherwise ignore.
apply(s,key,resource,delta): apply only when s is open and key has not appeared in its current epoch. Add delta to the resource balance and append an uncompensated ledger step. Otherwise ignore.
fail(s): change open to failed; otherwise ignore.
commit(s): change open to committed; otherwise ignore.
compensate(s): apply only when failed. Visit uncompensated current-epoch steps in reverse order, subtract each delta from its resource, mark each compensated, then set status=compensated. Otherwise ignore.
restart(s): apply only when committed or compensated. Increment epoch, set status=open, and replace the epoch-local ledger with empty. Resource balances persist. Otherwise ignore.
Event acknowledgements expose applied/ignored and sequence but hide balances and saga ledgers.
audit(resources,sagas) returns compact JSON with requested resources sorted by the requested order; requested saga records include saga,status,epoch,applied_count,compensated_count,current_uncompensated_delta_sum. It also returns selected_balance_sum and selected_uncompensated_delta_sum. JSON object-key and requested-record order are not semantic because resource/saga identifiers are explicit. No unstated side effects exist.

MULTI-RESOURCE QUOTA CONTRACT v1.
The world starts empty. register(resource,policy,config) creates a resource
once. policy is component, weighted, or burst. component config is exact
nonnegative limits for cpu,memory,io. weighted config is exact positive
integer weights for those dimensions plus a nonnegative budget. burst config
is exact nonnegative base limits plus a nonnegative shared burst_pool.

allocate(id,resource,amounts) checks, in this exact order: resource exists;
all and only cpu,memory,io are positive integers; id is new; resource is not
frozen; and the resource's policy admits the resulting total active usage.
component admits iff every dimension is within its limit, checking dimensions
in cpu,memory,io order. weighted admits iff the sum across dimensions of
resulting_usage*weight is at most budget. burst admits iff the sum across
dimensions of max(0,resulting_usage-base_limit) is at most burst_pool. A
successful allocation records the amounts. release(id) removes a known active
allocation. freeze/unfreeze toggle a known resource and ignore a repeated
state. set_limit(resource,dimension,value) changes one component or burst base
limit. set_weight changes one weighted weight and requires a positive value.
set_budget changes a weighted budget. set_burst changes a burst pool. Config
changes retain usage, which may leave the resource over quota.

The exact allocation reasons are unknown_resource, invalid_amounts,
duplicate_id, frozen, or quota_exceeded. A hypothetical request is read-only
and returns the exact current usage and policy config, allowed, reason, and
binding: the first exceeded dimension for component, weighted_budget for
weighted, burst_pool for burst, otherwise null.

id, resource, amounts, usage, config, allowed, reason, and binding in that
schema. JSON object-key order is nonsemantic. No unstated defaults exist.

DYNAMIC DEPENDENCY DAG CONTRACT v1.
The nodes are exactly the 48 entity names introduced by the init events below. Their two-digit numeric suffix defines the order: suffix 00 < ... < suffix 47, regardless of any domain prefix such as service-, resource-, case-, sample-, or artifact-node-. Each node has integer base, value, revision, and dirty. Directed weighted edges may only go from a lower-suffix node to a higher-suffix node, so the graph is acyclic.
init(n,b): base=value=b mod 997, revision=0, dirty=false.
link(p,c,w): require p<c; insert or replace edge p->c with weight w mod 997, then mark c and every transitive descendant dirty.
unlink(p,c): if the edge exists remove it and mark c and every transitive descendant dirty; otherwise ignore.
set_base(n,b): set base=b mod 997, increment n.revision, and mark n plus every transitive descendant dirty.
recompute(n): apply only when every direct parent is clean. Set value=(base + sum(parent.value*edge_weight)) mod 997, set dirty=false, increment revision. Otherwise ignore.
